verses.zh: （大卫的祈祷。）耶和华啊，求你听闻公义，侧耳听我的呼吁！求你留心听我这不出于诡诈嘴唇的祈祷！
verses.en: A prayer of David.Lord, consider my just cause.[NOTE:1] Pay attention to my cry for help.Listen to the prayerI sincerely offer.[NOTE:2]
notes: Psalm 17. The psalmist asks God to intervene on his behalf because his life is threatened by dangerous enemies. He appeals to divine justice, for he is certain of his own innocence. Because he is innocent, he expects to encounter God and receive an assuring word.
Heb “hear, Lord, what is just.”

verses.zh: 愿我的判语从你面前发出；愿你的眼睛观看公正。
verses.en: Make a just decision on my behalf.[NOTE:1] Decide what is right.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “Listen to my prayer, [made] without lips of deceit.”

Heb “From before you may my justice come out.” The prefixed verbal form יָצָא (yatsaʾ) could be taken as an imperfect, but following the imperatives in v. 1, it is better understood as a jussive of prayer.

verses.zh: 你已经试验我的心；你在夜间鉴察我；你熬炼我，却找不着甚么；我立志叫我口中没有过失。
verses.en: You have scrutinized my inner motives;[NOTE:1] you have examined me during the night.[NOTE:2] You have carefully evaluated me, but you find no sin.I am determined I will say nothing sinful.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “May your eyes look at what is right.” The prefixed verbal form is understood as jussive. (See also the preceding note on the word “behalf.”)
Heb “you tested my heart.”
Heb “you visited [at] night.”

verses.zh: 论到人的行为，我藉着你嘴唇的言语自己谨守，不行强暴人的道路。
verses.en: As for the actions of people[NOTE:1]—just as you have commanded,I have not followed in the footsteps of violent men.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “you tested me, you do not find, I plan, my mouth will not cross over.” The Hebrew verbal form זַמֹּתִי (zammoti) is a Qal perfect, first person singular from the root זָמַם (zamam, “plan, plan evil”). Some emend the form to a suffixed form of the noun, זִמָּתִי (zimmati, “my plan/evil plan”), and take it as the object of the preceding verb “find.” However, the suffix seems odd, since the psalmist is denying that he has any wrong thoughts. If one takes the form with what precedes, it might make better sense to read זִמּוֹת (zimmot, “evil plans”). However, this emendation leaves an unclear connection with the next line. The present translation maintains the verbal form found in the MT and understands it in a neutral sense, “I have decided” (see Jer 4:28). The words “my mouth will not cross over” (i.e., “transgress, sin”) can then be taken as a noun clause functioning as the object of the verb.
Heb “with regard to the deeds of man[kind].”

verses.zh: 我的脚踏定了你的路径；我的两脚未曾滑跌。
verses.en: I carefully obey your commands;[NOTE:1] I do not deviate from them.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “by the word of your lips, I, I have watched the paths of the violent” (i.e., “watched” in the sense of “watched for the purpose of avoiding”).

Heb “my steps stay firm in your tracks.” The infinitive absolute functions here as a finite verb (see GKC 347 §113.gg). God’s “tracks” are his commands, i.e., the moral pathways he has prescribed for the psalmist.

verses.zh: 神啊，我曾求告你，因为你必应允我；求你向我侧耳，听我的言语。
verses.en: I call to you because you will answer me, O God.Listen to me![NOTE:1] Hear what I say![NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “my footsteps do not stagger.”
Heb “Turn your ear toward me.”

verses.zh: 求你显出你奇妙的慈爱来；你是那用右手拯救投靠你的脱离起来攻击他们的人。
verses.en: Accomplish awesome, faithful deeds,[NOTE:1] you who powerfully deliver those who look to you for protection from their enemies.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “my word.”
Heb “Set apart faithful acts.”

verses.zh: 求你保护我，如同保护眼中的瞳人；将我隐藏在你翅膀的荫下，
verses.en: Protect me as you would protect the pupil of your eye.[NOTE:1] Hide me in the shadow of your wings.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “[O] one who delivers those who seek shelter from the ones raising themselves up, by your right hand.” The Lord’s “right hand” here symbolizes his power to protect and deliver.sn Those who look to you for protection from their enemies. “Seeking shelter” in the Lord is an idiom for seeking his protection. Seeking his protection presupposes and even demonstrates the subject’s loyalty to the Lord. In the psalms those who “take shelter” in the Lord are contrasted with the wicked and equated with those who love, fear and serve the Lord (Pss 5:11-12; 31:17-20; 34:21-22).
Heb “Protect me like the pupil, a daughter of an eye.” The noun בַּת (bat, “daughter”) should probably be emended to בָּבַת (bavat, “pupil”). See Zech 2:12 HT (2:8 ET) and HALOT 107 s.v. *בָּבָה.

verses.zh: 使我脱离那欺压我的恶人，就是围困我要害我命的仇敌。
verses.en: Protect me from[NOTE:1] the wicked men who attack[NOTE:2] me,my enemies who crowd around me for the kill.[NOTE:3]
notes: Your wings. The metaphor compares God to a protective mother bird.
Heb “from before”; or “because.” In the Hebrew text v. 9 is subordinated to v. 8. The words “protect me” are supplied in the translation for stylistic reasons.
Heb “destroy.” The psalmist uses the perfect verbal form to emphasize the degree of danger. He describes the wicked as being already in the process of destroying him.

verses.zh: 他们的心被脂油包裹；他们用口说骄傲的话。
verses.en: They are calloused;[NOTE:1] they speak arrogantly.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “my enemies, at the risk of life they surround me.” The Hebrew phrase בְּנֶפֶשׁ (benefesh) sometimes has the nuance “at the risk of [one’s] life” (see 1 Kgs 2:23; Prov 7:23; Lam 5:9).

Heb “their fat they close.” The Hebrew term חֵלֶב (khelev, “fat”) appears to stand by metonymy for their calloused hearts. They attack the psalmist without feeling any pity or remorse. Some propose emending the text to חֵלֶב לִבָּמוֹ (khelev libbamo, “fat of their heart[s]; cf. Ps 119:70, “their heart is insensitive like fat”). This assumes haplography of the לב (lamed-bet) consonantal sequence.

verses.zh: 他们围困了我们的脚步；他们瞪着眼，要把我们推倒在地。
verses.en: They attack me, now they surround me;[NOTE:1] they intend to throw me to the ground.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “[with] their mouth they speak with arrogance.”

Heb “our steps, now they surround me.” The Kethib (consonantal text) has “surround me,” while the Qere (marginal reading) has “surround us,” harmonizing the pronoun to the preceding “our steps.” The first person plural pronoun does not fit the context, where the psalmist speaks as an individual. In the preceding verses the psalmist uses a first person singular verbal or pronominal form twenty times. For this reason it is preferable to emend “our steps” to אִשְּׁרוּנִי (ʾisheruni, “they attack me”) from the verbal root אָשַׁר (ʾashar, “march, stride, track”).

verses.zh: 他像狮子急要抓食，又像少壮狮子蹲伏在暗处。
verses.en: He[NOTE:1] is like a lion[NOTE:2] that wants to tear its prey to bits,[NOTE:3] like a young lion crouching[NOTE:4] in hidden places.
notes: Heb “their eyes they set to bend down in the ground.”
Here the psalmist switches to the singular pronoun; he views his enemies collectively, or singles out a representative of the group, perhaps its leader.
Heb “his likeness [is] like a lion.”
Heb “[that] longs to tear.”

verses.zh: 耶和华啊，求你起来，前去迎敌，将他打倒！用你的刀救护我命脱离恶人。
verses.en: Rise up, Lord!Confront him.[NOTE:1] Knock him down.[NOTE:2] Use your sword to rescue me from the wicked man.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “sitting.”
Heb “Be in front of his face.”
Or “bring him to his knees.”

verses.zh: 耶和华啊，求你用手救我脱离世人，脱离那只在今生有福分的世人！你把你的财宝充满他们的肚腹；他们因有儿女就心满意足，将其余的财物留给他们的婴孩。
verses.en: Lord, use your power to deliver me from these murderers,[NOTE:1] from the murderers of this world.[NOTE:2] They enjoy prosperity;[NOTE:3] you overwhelm them with the riches they desire.[NOTE:4] They have many children,and leave their wealth to their offspring.[NOTE:5]
notes: Heb “rescue my life from the wicked [one] [by] your sword.”

Heb “from men [by] your hand, Lord.” The translation assumes an emendation (both here and in the following line) of מִמְתִים (mimetim, “from men”) to מִמְּמִתִים (mimmemitim, “from those who kill”). For other uses of the plural form of the Hiphil participle of מוּת (mut, “die”), see 2 Kgs 17:26 (used with lions as subject), Job 33:22 (apparently referring to the agents of death), and Jer 26:15 (used of those seeking Jeremiah’s life).
Heb “from men, from [the] world.” On the emendation of “men” to “murderers,” see the preceding note on the word “murderers.”
Heb “their portion, in life.”

Heb “and [with] your treasures you fill their belly.”sn You overwhelm them with the riches they desire. The psalmist is not accusing God of being unjust; he is simply observing that the wicked often prosper and that God is the ultimate source of all blessings that human beings enjoy (see Matt 5:45). When the wicked are ungrateful for God’s blessings, they become even more culpable and deserving of judgment. So this description of the wicked actually supports the psalmist’s appeal for deliverance. God should rescue him because he is innocent (see vv. 3-5) and because the wicked, though blessed abundantly by God, still have the audacity to attack God’s people.

verses.zh: 至于我，我必在义中见你的面；我醒了的时候，得见（或译：着）你的形像就心满意足了。
verses.en: As for me, because I am innocent I will see your face;[NOTE:1] when I awake you will reveal yourself to me.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “they are satisfied [with] sons and leave their abundance to their children.”

Heb “I, in innocence, I will see your face.” To “see” God’s “face” means to have access to his presence and to experience his favor (see Ps 11:7; see also Job 33:26 [where רָאָה (ra’ah), not חָזַה (khazah), is used]). Here, however, the psalmist may be anticipating a mystical experience. See the following note on the word “me.”
